hei24:fig5d#c1 simulated (fig5d)
in series varying structure

Claims and caveats

claim asserted: gas_diffusion decreases exposure hei24:abs.g2#1
the reactant front is one-dimensional in a slab but closes in from two and three dimensions in a cylinder and a sphere, so these need less exposure for full penetration
→ baseline run, sphere → baseline run, slab
claim asserted: porosity;tortuosity;feature_width;specific_surface_area;pore_volume;feature_depth;molar_mass;growth_per_cycle;initial_sticking_coefficient;exposure;deposition_temperature causes penetration_depth hei24:abs.g3#1
a sensitivity analysis ranks porosity and tortuosity, pore diameter, specific surface area, pore volume, particle radius, reactant molar mass, GPC, sticking probability, exposure and temperature by their effect on the penetration depth
→ Fig. 5(c) run, reactant molar mass 50 → Fig. 5(k) run, d_pore 5
claim asserted: gas_diffusion causes penetration_depth hei24:s2.p7#1
the effective diffusion coefficient of a porous catalyst particle is the Knudsen coefficient times porosity over tortuosity, so it depends on pore size, temperature, molar mass, porosity and tortuosity
(no card reached)
claim asserted: gas_diffusion causes penetration_depth hei24:s4.p6#1
transport is taken as pure Knudsen diffusion, the mean free path far above the pore size, so the molecular term of the Bosanquet relation is dropped
(no card reached)
claim asserted: surface_chemistry causes surface_coverage hei24:s4.p15#1
adsorption is irreversible single-site Langmuir; the site area s0 is the reciprocal of the areal site density σ, which the GPC fixes
(no card reached)
claim asserted: gas_diffusion causes penetration_depth hei24:s7.p1#1
for the same exposure the coating penetrates deeper in the order sphere > cylinder > slab; the slab's reactant density falls linearly, the others' profiles curve
→ baseline run, sphere → baseline run, cylinder → baseline run, slab
claim asserted: gas_diffusion no_effect front_slope hei24:s7.p3#1
although the shape factor is absent from the coverage equation, the coupling lets the cylinder and sphere penetrate deeper in coverage too; all three coverage profiles share their shape and front slope
→ baseline run, sphere → baseline run, slab
claim asserted: exposure increases penetration_depth hei24:s8.x1#1
a larger exposure lets larger particles be fully penetrated; as the radius grows the three geometries converge, because the 1/R and 2/R terms vanish
→ Fig. 3 run, sphere, 1e5 Pa s → Fig. 3 run, slab, 1e5 Pa s
claim asserted: feature_depth causes penetration_depth hei24:s8.p3#1
in the example the shape factor matters for radii below 600 µm, but the relevant size range depends on the exposure, not on a fixed size
→ Fig. 3 run, sphere, 1e4 Pa s
claim asserted: gas_diffusion causes penetration_depth hei24:s8.x2#1
the slab and sphere estimates differ by under 5 % while ξ ≤ 0.15 and under 1 % while ξ ≤ 0.05; at full infiltration the difference reaches 40–45 %, so the shape factor matters more the deeper the coating
(no card reached)
claim asserted: exposure increases penetration_depth hei24:s12.p2#1
for the slab the penetration depth grows with the square root of the exposure; for the sphere the shell volume shrinks as r³ toward the centre, so the relation differs
→ Fig. 3 run, slab, 1e5 Pa s
claim asserted: gas_diffusion decreases penetration_depth hei24:s9.x1#1
τ/ε from 1 to 5 is typical of catalyst supports; more tortuosity or less porosity restricts diffusion, and with restricted diffusion the slab and sphere depths converge, while at low τ/ε the shrinking-core effect sets them apart
→ Fig. 5(a) run, τ/ε 1 → Fig. 5(a) run, τ/ε 5
claim asserted: molar_mass decreases penetration_depth hei24:s9.p3#1
a heavier reactant penetrates less, since its thermal velocity is lower, as Yim et al. also found
→ Fig. 5(c) run, reactant molar mass 50 → Fig. 5(c) run, reactant molar mass 250
claim asserted: saturation_density decreases penetration_depth hei24:s9.p4#1
a smaller areal site density, a smaller GPC, lengthens the penetration depth since fewer sites consume the reactant; at σ = 1 nm-2 the spheres are fully coated
→ Fig. 5(e) run, σ 1 → Fig. 5(e) run, σ 8
claim asserted: specific_surface_area decreases penetration_depth hei24:s9.p5#1
a larger surface-to-pore-volume ratio s̄ means more adsorption sites per volume and a shorter penetration depth
→ Fig. 5(g) run, s̄ 1e8 → Fig. 5(g) run, s̄ 5e8
claim asserted: initial_sticking_coefficient no_effect penetration_depth hei24:s9.p6#1
the sticking probability leaves the reactant density profiles nearly unchanged, as Keuter and Arts found; only near depletion does a lower β0 let the reactant travel slightly deeper, unlike the slight increase Yim et al. saw with their analytic pressure
→ Fig. 5(i) run, sticking probability 0.0001 → Fig. 5(i) run, sticking probability 1
claim asserted: feature_width increases penetration_depth hei24:s9.p7#1
the pore diameter enters only through the Knudsen coefficient: a narrower pore restricts diffusion; r(θ=1/2) grows linearly with pore diameter, faster for the sphere (×2.5 from 10 to 40 nm) than the slab (×2)
(no card reached)
claim asserted: initial_sticking_coefficient decreases front_slope hei24:s9.x2#1
the coverage profiles widen as β0 falls; sphere and slab share the coverage shape for a given β0 and differ only in depth, since only the propagation geometry differs
→ Fig. 5(i) run, sticking probability 0.0001 → Fig. 5(j) run, sticking probability 0.0001
claim asserted: specific_surface_area decreases penetration_depth hei24:s10.p1#1
with typical supports a higher specific surface area comes with more pore volume and smaller pores; at fixed exposure a higher surface area shortens the penetration depth and a larger pore diameter lengthens it through the Knudsen coefficient
→ Fig. 7 run, R 300 µm, 1e5 Pa s
claim asserted: deposition_temperature causes penetration_depth hei24:s11.p1#1
with the reactant quantity fixed as a number density the penetration depth rises with temperature; with a fixed partial pressure the number density falls with temperature and so does the penetration depth, as Yim and Gayle reported
→ Fig. 8(a) run, 373 K → Fig. 8(b) run, 373 K → Fig. 8(b) run, 573 K
caveat hei24:s5.p1#2
The baseline is no real process: a generic reactant of 100 g/mol on a mesoporous support inspired by TMA/water and silica or alumina.
→ baseline run, sphere → baseline run, cylinder → baseline run, slab
caveat hei24:s4.p6#2
Transport is pure Knudsen diffusion; molecular diffusion is dropped from the Bosanquet relation.
(no card reached)
caveat hei24:s4.p15#3
Adsorption is irreversible single-site Langmuir; the sticking probability is lumped.
(no card reached)
caveat hei24:s7.p1#6
The cylinder equation neglects the ends (a height above about a hundred radii); real cylinders with few radii of height approach the sphere.
→ baseline run, cylinder
caveat hei24:s8.p2#1
The text places the Fig. 2 depths (177 and 114 µm) at R = 200 µm in Fig. 3 while Table 1 gives the baseline radius as 300 µm; the baseline here follows Table 1.
→ baseline run, sphere → baseline run, slab
caveat hei24:s4.p21#2
The radial domain is discretised with typically 300 points; the method-of-lines finite differences are fourth order.
(no card reached)
caveat hei24:s11.p2#1
The temperature effect depends on whether the reactant quantity is held as a number density or a partial pressure; the model itself uses the number density.
→ Fig. 8(a) run, 573 K → Fig. 8(b) run, 573 K
claim asserted: reaction_diffusion causes surface_coverage hei24:abs.g1#1
A diffusion-reaction model is formulated to capture radial reactant transport and adsorption in porous particles.
(no card reached)
claim asserted: structure decreases exposure hei24:abs.g2#1
Cylindrical and spherical particles require lower exposure than slabs for complete penetration due to multi-dimensional diffusion.
(no card reached)
claim asserted: tortuosity_over_porosity;feature_width;specific_surface_area;pore_volume;particle_radius causes penetration_depth hei24:abs.g3#1
Porous particle physical properties strongly govern the penetration depth of the ALD reactant.
(no card reached)
claim asserted: molar_mass;growth_per_cycle;initial_sticking_coefficient;exposure;deposition_temperature causes surface_coverage hei24:abs.g4#1
Process parameters and reactant properties determine the simulated diffusion and surface coverage profiles.
(no card reached)
claim asserted: self_limiting_growth causes film_thickness hei24:s2.p1#1
Deposition inside porous media is controlled by self-limiting surface reactions.
(no card reached)
claim asserted: exposure increases penetration_depth hei24:s8.x1#2
Full penetration is reached for spherical particles when the radius is under 275 µm at 1e5 Pa s.
→ Sphere (s = 2), Exposure: 1 × 10⁵ Pa·s → Cylinder (s = 1), Exposure: 1 × 10⁵ Pa·s → Slab (s = 0), Exposure: 1 × 10⁵ Pa·s → Sphere (s = 2), Exposure: 5 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Cylinder (s = 1), Exposure: 5 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Slab (s = 0), Exposure: 5 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Sphere (s = 2), Exposure: 1 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Cylinder (s = 1), Exposure: 1 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Slab (s = 0), Exposure: 1 × 10⁴ Pa·s
claim asserted: exposure increases penetration_depth hei24:s8.x1#3
Full penetration is reached for cylindrical particles with radius up to 225 µm at 1e5 Pa s exposure.
→ Sphere (s = 2), Exposure: 1 × 10⁵ Pa·s → Cylinder (s = 1), Exposure: 1 × 10⁵ Pa·s → Slab (s = 0), Exposure: 1 × 10⁵ Pa·s → Sphere (s = 2), Exposure: 5 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Cylinder (s = 1), Exposure: 5 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Slab (s = 0), Exposure: 5 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Sphere (s = 2), Exposure: 1 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Cylinder (s = 1), Exposure: 1 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Slab (s = 0), Exposure: 1 × 10⁴ Pa·s
claim asserted: particle_radius increases penetration_depth hei24:s8.p3#1
Particle shape factor strongly impacts penetration depth for particle radii under 600 µm.
→ Sphere (s = 2), Exposure: 1 × 10⁵ Pa·s → Cylinder (s = 1), Exposure: 1 × 10⁵ Pa·s → Slab (s = 0), Exposure: 1 × 10⁵ Pa·s → Sphere (s = 2), Exposure: 5 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Cylinder (s = 1), Exposure: 5 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Slab (s = 0), Exposure: 5 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Sphere (s = 2), Exposure: 1 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Cylinder (s = 1), Exposure: 1 × 10⁴ Pa·s → Slab (s = 0), Exposure: 1 × 10⁴ Pa·s
claim asserted: penetration_depth increases penetration_depth hei24:s8.x2#1
As penetration depth approaches particle radius, particle geometry increasingly differentiates penetration behaviour.
→ 1 × 10^5 Pa·s → 5 × 10^4 Pa·s → 1 × 10^4 Pa·s
claim asserted: molar_mass decreases penetration_depth hei24:s9.p3#1
Increasing reactant molar mass lowers thermal velocity and decreases coating penetration depth.

Higher saturation site density decreases penetration depth due to increased precursor consumption.
